chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The habitual (drinker) of wine is like an idol worshipper.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise analogy to highlight that habitual wine consumption (mudmin) leads to a state of spiritual alienation comparable to idol worship, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the nullification of prayer. This comparison underscores the transformative effect of chronic intoxication on the soul's connection to the Divine, serving as a critical ethical benchmark for believers. The hadith thus elevates the prohibition from mere ritual impurity to a profound metaphysical shift in one's spiritual status.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The habitual (drinker of) the wine is like an idol worshipper’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A wine addict is like a worshipper of idols.’”
